plans.direction: Evolve the single hook `score_ruin_nodes` as a multiplicative gated rank-power destroy-selection rule, with the rank exponent p made state-adaptive: p small (≈0.5–0.8, near-uniform randomized-agnostic spread) during early low-`iter_frac` exploration and p ramping up (≈1.5–2.0, sharp worst-removal focus) as `stagnation_ratio` grows. Gate by load utilization, depot proximity of the customer nearest in route, demand magnitude and route-length share, so that the ruin set prefers customers whose removal unlocks load re-balancing across routes. Keep the repair side fixed (deterministic Regret-2 + local intra_2opt + R2R acceptance) and keep the hook fully deterministic and state-only, so the gain is attributable to destroy prioritization alone under the 2000 ms budget where many more LNS iterations fit than the 500 ms reference.
plans.hypothesis: Under a 2000 ms per-instance budget the L3 ruin-recreate skeleton performs far more iterations than at 500 ms; therefore a stagnation-adaptive rank-power destroy score (near-uniform ruin early to diversify, sharp worst-cost ruin under stagnation, multiplied by load/depot/demand/route-share gates) will beat the zero-evolution Worst-Cost-Removal control on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 by a larger margin than the +0.12% seen at 500 ms, because extra iterations amplify the value of a destroy policy that escapes local minima while never discarding high-`removal_savings` structural targets.

operations.mechanism: Archive is empty (solver_count=0, no known signatures), so this round should establish the round-1 baseline on the mandated interface. The KB method entry (method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3, content_sha256 94f7d539…) fixes the skeleton — CW + initial intra_2opt, Ruin(top-q) -> deterministic Regret-2 -> local intra_2opt -> R2R acceptance — and confirms `score_ruin_nodes` is the only evolvable hook with a multiplicative gate × rank-power form: score_i = rank_power(|removal_savings_i|/scale * gate_load * gate_depot * gate_demand * gate_rdist, p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio)). Its blameworthy regime is the tight 25 ms budget (120/120 early-stop), and our target budget is 2000 ms — the mirror-image regime where first_feasible_ms ≈ 2–3 ms leaves nearly the whole budget for LNS iterations, so the anytime-curve payoff of a better destroy policy is maximal. Postprocess is fixed to `none` per the allowed set, and the repair layer stays untouched so any delta vs L3-ctrl is cleanly attributable to the evolved destroy score. Regret-2 feasibility handling follows method-cvrp-cheapest-regret-insertion, ensuring the 5-gate validator's dual-action probe (first_ruin_set A={1,2,3,4} vs B={3,4,5,6} on n=6, q=4) is satisfied by strict determinism and no global RNG.

plans.direction: Densify the destroy score into a two-component mixed operator: keep the round-2 multiplicative gates (removal savings / depot-distance / route-load saturation) but add a Shaw-style spatial-relatedness term (customer's mean distance to the k nearest other customers, normalized — high for isolated customers, low inside tight clusters) plus a deterministic index-hash jitter, so that on clustered/loose-capacity instances removal alternates between isolated outliers and cluster interiors instead of repeatedly picking the same high-savings ring, with the stagnation-driven rank exponent now modulating the savings-vs-relatedness mix ratio rather than only the tail rank.
plans.hypothesis: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 2000 ms, augmenting the round-2 supported destroy score with a normalized Shaw spatial-relatedness term and a deterministic index-hash jitter, with the stagnation-driven rank power re-pointed at modulating the savings-vs-relatedness blend (diversified mid-tail removal under stagnation) will lower mean objective below the round-2 record 16.078067, with the largest per-instance gains on the reported weakest regimes (spatial=clustered, depot_style=eccentric, size=100, capacity_level=loose), because the round-2 gains came from gate concentration and now saturate (round-2 vs round-1 delta only -0.0516, archive gap_over_sbs 0.19%), so the remaining headroom is in removal-set diversity rather than in severity of savings ranking.

operations.mechanism: Archive shows two nearly identical L3 solvers (16.1297 / 16.0781) with vbs-sbs gap of only 0.1937%, i.e. the current destroy rule is near a local attractor and further pure re-weighting of savings gates yields diminishing returns; the round-2 hypothesis already confirmed that gated ranking + stagnation rank power works, so round 3 attacks removal-SET diversity (Shaw relatedness mixing + deterministic jitter, RNG-free to keep determinism) which the KB entry method-cvrp-lns-shaw-regret identifies as the standard complement to worst-removal in LNS, while keeping the fixed Regret-2 repair and unified deadline invariants of the verified L3 skeleton (first_feasible_ms ~2-3 ms, solve_ms_mean 108 ms leaves ample headroom within 2000 ms).

plans.direction: Refine the round-2 champion destroy score (method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3) into a scale-free, stagnation-phase-scheduled ruin rule: keep the multiplicative gates (normalized removal savings x depot-distance gate x route-load saturation gate) but (i) replace the single fixed rank exponent with a two-phase schedule that is near-linear-greedy at iter_frac<0.35 and transitions to a mid-tail power (p~0.5-0.7) plus a small deterministic jitter term later, (ii) add a 'route-sparsity' factor 1/(route_len) so short/degenerate routes are prioritized for rearrangement, and (iii) add a Shaw-relatedness term to the second ruin pass (customers near the already-selected seed customer score higher) so successive removals in the same iteration cluster geographically instead of scattering. Hyperparameter sensitivity (gate strengths, phase switch point, power bounds) is co-evolved, not hand-tuned.
plans.hypothesis: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 2000 ms, replacing the round-2 fixed gate/rank-power destroy score with (a) an iter_frac-scheduled two-phase rank exponent, (b) a route-sparsity (short-route priority) factor and (c) a Shaw-relatedness second-pass term will lower mean objective below the current SBS 16.078067, with the largest per-instance gains on the weakest regimes (size 100, loose capacity, eccentric depot, uniform demand), because those instances have many partially-filled short routes whose customers are geographically interchangeable and thus need spatially coherent removal rather than globally top-savings removal.

operations.mechanism: Archive shows only 3 near-identical solvers (16.0781 / 16.0931 / 16.1297) with gap_over_vbs of just 0.37%, so the remaining headroom is small and must be won by fine-grained destroy-priority structure rather than a new paradigm. KB entry method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 documents that the multiplicative gated-savings + stagnation rank-power rule is the verified-best hook for this exact interface (23.3186 vs 23.3474 L3-ctrl on blind_120) and lists 'stagnation_aware_diversification' as its strong regime, while method-cvrp-lns-shaw-regret establishes that relatedness-based destroy (Shaw) is the standard complementary diversification operator under LNS. Combining them inside the single allowed hook (score_ruin_nodes) keeps the deterministic Regret-2 recreate, intra_2opt and R2R acceptance untouched, so any measured delta is attributable to the destroy policy. Phase-scheduled greediness avoids the early-search waste of always randomized removal and the late-search trap of always-greedy removal, and the route-sparsity factor targets exactly the loose-capacity/size-100 regimes flagged as weakest in archive_feedback.

plans.direction: Refine the round-4 champion destroy score from a multiplicative depot-load gate into a capacity-slack-aware, route-sparsity-normalized score with a three-phase stagnation clock: (1) exploit phase — concentrate removals on the smallest routes (fewest stops, highest residual capacity) to enable route-elimination moves; (2) neutral phase — flat rank power over normalized removal savings; (3) diversify phase — randomized mid-tail removal driven by Shaw relatedness to the last-improved incumbent. All gates remain scale-invariant (normalized by mean depot distance) and deterministic, with tie-breaks by index only.
plans.hypothesis: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 2000 ms with cvrp_ruin_recreate/none, replacing the round-4 fixed depot+load gate with a capacity-slack x route-sparsity gate (score = |savings|/scale * (1 + alpha * slack_frac) * (1 + beta / n_stops) * depot_gate) and a three-phase stagnation clock (exploit -> neutral -> Shaw-diversify) will lower mean objective below the 15.9801 SBS, with the largest per-instance gains in the weakest regimes (tight capacity, size 100, eccentric depot, clustered spatial), because route-elimination-friendly removals are most valuable exactly where capacity is binding and geometry is clustered.

operations.mechanism: Round-4 already validated the normalized-savings x depot-gate x route-load-gate core plus a two-phase rank schedule (mean 15.980136 vs SBS 16.078067, all 24/24 feasible, solve_ms 207.9 ms — only ~10% of the 2000 ms budget, so there is ample headroom for a richer hook without any timeout risk). Two structural weaknesses remain: (a) the load gate only penalizes near-capacity routes, giving no explicit bonus to the small/degenerate routes whose removal can eliminate a whole vehicle, which is where tight-capacity instances (vbs_rel_gap -22.7%) lose most; (b) the two-phase rank schedule jumps from greedy to mid-tail without an explicit relatedness term, so diversification is spatially blind. The KB L3 blueprint confirms the interface invariant (finite length-n float vector, read-only state, deterministic tie-breaks, no global RNG) and the Shaw entry supplies the relatedness metric, while the regret-insertion entry confirms the fixed Regret-2 repair stays untouched. Budget headroom (208 ms used of 2000 ms) means added per-call cost is safe; expect < 400 ms mean even with the extra vectorized terms. Postprocess stays none to preserve the 5-gate interface and avoid any extra unmapped stage.

plans.direction: Capacity-slack-aware multi-scale ruin scope with cluster-coherent sector destruction and stagnation-triggered tail randomization, dedicated to tight-capacity / clustered / eccentric-depot / size-100 regimes.
plans.hypothesis: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 2000 ms, a score_ruin_nodes that (a) rescales normalized removal savings by a capacity-slack factor raised to an iter_frac-scheduled exponent so that near-full routes (load/Q > 0.9) are progressively shielded while slack-rich routes stay destroyable early, (b) adds a sector-coherence term keyed on |cos(angle to depot)| and radial distance so ruin sets stay spatially contiguous on clustered geometries, and (c) injects a stagnation_ratio-driven randomized mid-tail component (rank exponent rising from ~0 to ~1.5 on stagnation) will lower the mean objective below the round-5 SBS of 15.8374, with the largest absolute reductions on tight-capacity, clustered-spatial, eccentric-depot and size-100 instances, since the existing rule's uniform load gating mis-sizes ruin scope when capacity slack is the binding constraint.

operations.mechanism: Round-5 confirmed (h_r2_ruin_depot_load_gate_rankpower supported) that normalized-savings x depot-gate x load/sparsity-gate with a stagnation rank schedule beats L3-ctrl (15.8374 vs 16.0781 SBS, all 24 feasible, 196 ms mean so ~10x headroom under the 2000 ms budget). Archive weakest regimes are tightly clustered: capacity_level=tight (rel gap -23.07%), size=100 (-21.78%), uniform demand (-21.53%), eccentric depot (-20.76%), clustered spatial (-19.98%), with zero exhausted/failed instances — so the loss is structural quality, not budget starvation. The KB L3 blueprint (method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3) prescribes exactly the multiplicative gate x rank-power ruin score and lists stagnation-aware diversification as its strong regime, and Shaw-relatedness ruin (method-cvrp-lns-shaw-regret) motivates spatial contiguity of destroy sets for clustered instances. Therefore this round converts the regime-concentration clause into a testable, targeted mechanism: replace the binary load gate with a continuous capacity-slack exponent schedule and add angular/radial sector coherence, keeping the deterministic Regret-2 recreation, intra_2opt polish and R2R acceptance fixed so any delta is attributable to the destroy hook alone.

plans.direction: Refine the round-7 supported destroy score into a saturation-normalized form: keep the multiplicative depot-distance gate and stale-route load gate but (a) rescale each route's load gate by the *instance-observed* mean route saturation (mean(route_loads)/capacity) so the gate's slope adapts to tight-capacity instances instead of using a fixed exponent, and (b) drive the rank exponent from stagnation only (p = 1.25 + 1.0*stagnation_ratio, no additive slack term, no sector-coherence term). Target: cut the tight-capacity / size-100 / eccentric-depot residual gap (currently ~21-23% VBS-relative) without perturbing the clustered regime where round-7 is already SBS-co-equal.
plans.hypothesis: On cvrp_dev_hetero_24 at 2000 ms, replacing the fixed load-saturation gate exponent with a self-normalizing exponent gamma = 1 + clip(mean_route_saturation - 0.5, 0, 0.4), applied as gate_load = (1 - route_loads/capacity)^gamma * (1 + 0.5*route_dists/mean(route_dists)), and setting the stagnation rank power to p = 1.25 + 1.0*stagnation_ratio with no additive slack term, will lower mean objective below the round-7 SBS 15.8554 (and the round-5 15.8374 frontier) because tight-capacity instances (12/24 of the suite) receive a steeper under-load emphasis that concentrates ruin on degenerate near-empty routes, while clustered/eccentric instances are unaffected by the exponent change since their mean saturation is near 0.5.

operations.mechanism: Round-7 (agent_artifacts/round_0007_dev_eval.json, sha256 29d2981...) confirmed the multiplicative depot-gate x load-gate x rank-power rule at 15.8554, statistically co-equal with the round-5 frontier 15.8374 and clearly above the 16.078 L3-ctrl baseline; that round also proved that adding engine terms (round-6 additive slack exponent + sector gate) costs 0.061. KB method-cvrp-m3-ruin-recreate-l3 documents the hook contract (score_ruin_nodes -> rank_power(|savings|/scale * gate_load * gate_depot * gate_demand * gate_rdist, p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio))) with output-length-n finite float invariant, so this proposal only re-parameterizes two multiplicative factors inside that verified skeleton. The change is a one-parameter-per-gate perturbation rather than a structural addition, so it is falsifiable: if mean objective does not drop below 15.8374 the self-normalizing saturation exponent claim fails and we revert to the frozen round-5/7 form. Weakest regimes from archive feedback (capacity_level=tight 12 instances, size=100 12 instances, eccentric depot 12 instances, clustered 8 instances) motivate the saturation-adaptive slope as the highest-leverage remaining knob.
